Interesting. Is that what cookies are? Sorry, I'm computer illiterate. I mean I get that some information is stored by my browser/computer to make the running of certain programs go more smoothly, but does that mean that all info is downloaded as a whole like a PDF?

Generally speaking, yes it is downloaded as a whole and stored on your computer in a temporary directory that gets cleaned out based on your settings. Sometimes smaller files never get cleaned out because that storage space isn't being required. The major exception is video, which in modern browsers can be streamed in chunks (which is why you can see the progress bar loading in) so you aren't downloading the whole video just to view a portion of it.

Cookies are small chunks of information, and are generally used to identify the web browser each time it connects to a website. If you customize a site, (for example, Voat) so that it is in dark mode, then Voat plants a cookie in your browser so that the next time you visit it knows your browser wants dark mode. Cookies can contain all kinds of information. The main goal of most cookies is to store a token after you type your username and password. This is how a website knows not to ask for it every time you click on something. Again using Voat as an example, you log in once and you can comment, browse, create threads, etc. Each time you click a link, Voat asks your browser, "What's the username and password" and your browser replies with, "I don't need it, I have this token". This is obviously a convenience as a user.

The nefarious part is that there are ways for websites to see what cookies you are storing in your browser. That way a tracking company (like Google) can see where you have been, what interests you have, etc. That is why the UK changed the law regarding use of cookies, and why every site you visit now has a notification letting you know they use cookies.
